research:
I couldn't open any article page directly, because the proxy refused every WebFetch call. Everything below comes from search-result snippets, and some of those are secondary or low-confidence. I left out everything dated after 2026-09-07.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-04: CL=F (Yahoo Finance, NYMEX front-month WTI) closed at 91.48, according to the code-collected data. I couldn't load the Yahoo page myself.
- Contract roll: CL=F follows the front month. The October 2026 contract (CLV6) normally expires around Sept 22, so on Oct 5 CL=F should be tracking the November contract (CLX6). I couldn't confirm the November-October spread. If the curve is in backwardation, as is typical in a supply shock, CL=F would drop mechanically at the roll.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the outcome yet. WTI is near $91-92, the highest in about six weeks, and is moving on US-Iran fighting around the Strait of Hormuz.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-07: Oil rose to about a six-week high as US-Iran strikes in the Strait of Hormuz intensified. WTI was up 79 cents at $92.27. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/7/oil-prices-surge-as-us-iran-strikes-intensify-in-strait-of-hormuz)
- 2026-09-06: Eight OPEC+ countries (the release lists seven) kept October production at September levels. Their next meeting is Oct 4. [OPEC](https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/1835613-6-september-2026.html), [Hellenic Shipping News](https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/saudi-arabia-russia-iraq-kuwait-kazakhstan-algeria-and-oman-reaffirm-commitment-to-market-stability/)
- 2026-09-04: Oil fell on Friday but was on track for weekly gains of about 10% for WTI and about 7% for Brent, driven by renewed US-Iran military exchanges. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-prices-ease-near-six-085140719.html)
- 2026-09-04: A low-confidence source puts Brent at $95.04 and says WTI topped $90, with Hormuz throughput down about 77% since late 2025, or roughly one fifth of pre-war levels. [Eastern Herald](https://easternherald.com/2026/09/04/brent-crude-oil-price-september-4-2026-hormuz-opec/)
- 2026-09-01/02: Per the search snippet, WTI settled at $90.22 on Sept 1 after a 5.2% jump on fresh US and Iranian strikes, then traded flat near $90.51 on Sept 2. Two tankers were disabled by mines, but a recovery in actual Hormuz transit limited the spike. [EnergyNow](https://energynow.com/2026/09/oil-holds-near-five-week-highs-as-u-s-iran-fighting-keeps-hormuz-risk-elevated/)
- 2026-08-28: WTI was about $82.52 after falling that day, and traded between $78.55 and $84.70 that week. Optimism about US-Iran talks faded, and Gulf producers were moving oil around Hormuz through ship-to-ship transfers and alternate pipelines. [Oil and Gas 360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/iran-diplomacy/), [PennWell](https://pennwellbooks.com/blogs/energy-insights/hormuz-bypass-tactics-push-oil-prices-lower)
- 2026-08 (August STEO): The EIA forecast a 2026 average of $86.81 for Brent and $80.88 for WTI, and estimated Middle East shut-ins at 5.5 mb/d in July. Hormuz flows averaged 4.9 mb/d in Q2 2026, against 21.6 mb/d in Q4 2025. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/aug26.pdf), [S&P Global](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/crude-oil/081126-us-eia-raises-brent-outlook-to-87b-on-hormuz-shipping-constraints)

## 4. Base rates
- Code-computed distribution of 21-trading-day outcomes from 91.48: p5 78.36, p10 82.77, p25 86.49, p50 91.21, p75 96.88, p90 102.97, p95 115.82.
- 2026 has been extremely volatile:
  - 2026-04-07/08: WTI fell 16.8% in one session, by $18.95 to $94.00, on a ceasefire. [Idaho Business Review](https://idahobusinessreview.com/2026/04/08/oil-falls-below-100-after-trump-iran-ceasefire/)
  - 2026-05-25: July WTI fell 6.5% to $90.31 on talk of a ceasefire extension. [Asiae](https://view.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026052606442250181)
  - One undated report says WTI fell 14.26% after Iran declared Hormuz open to all ships. [SJV Sun](https://sjvsun.com/?p=104330)
- Recent trend: WTI went from about $82.5 on Aug 28 to about $92 on Sept 7, roughly +11% in one week.
- The pattern is that diplomatic headlines have brought single-day drops of 6-17%, and escalations have brought jumps of 5-10% in a week.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-26: The Polymarket "What will WTI hit in September 2026" market (a touch market, not a closing price) had "↓$80" at about 72%, with about $18K volume. That snapshot is stale and was taken before the September rally. [PredScope](https://predscope.com/event/what-price-will-wti-hit-in-september-2026)
- Commonwealth Bank of Australia: restoring 50-60% of pre-war Hormuz flows could push Brent toward the low end of its $70-100 range (date unclear). [PennWell](https://pennwellbooks.com/blogs/energy-insights/hormuz-bypass-tactics-push-oil-prices-lower)
- I couldn't find a current Kalshi or Manifold contract for Oct 5, or any bank forecast published in early September.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The US-Iran conflict and Hormuz: strikes, mines, attacks on tankers and Navy ships, and any ceasefire or reopening talks. This is the main driver in both directions.
- About Sept 9: the EIA September STEO. Also the OPEC and IEA monthly oil market reports in mid-September.
- Weekly EIA inventory reports every Wednesday.
- Around Sept 16-17: the FOMC meeting.
- Around Sept 22: the October WTI contract expires and CL=F rolls to November.
- Oct 4 (Sunday): the OPEC+ eight-country meeting sets November output. Oil would first react to it in trading on Oct 5, the resolution date.
- Hurricane season peaks in the Gulf of Mexico.
